Today you'll head to the highland market in Chichicastenango with an English-speaking guide. The visit is possible on Thursdays or Sundays.

Before the Spanish conquest, the town was known as Chaviar and was an important Kaqchikel trading centre. Surrounded by valleys and mountains, the town is known for its mist, cobbled streets and red-tiled roofs. On market days, vendors and travellers come from across the country.

The Sunday market is bigger. That day, the cofradías, or religious brotherhoods, hold processions inside and around the Church of Santo Tomás. The church was built in 1540 in honour of the town's patron saint. On the way to the cemetery stands another Catholic church, El Calvario.

Chichicastenango is known for its textiles and masks. You can pay at the market in US dollars or by credit card.

Overnight at Hotel Porto Antigua in a Standard double room, with breakfast included.
Stacks of brightly coloured striped fabric at Chichicastenango Market, Guatemala

Take a walking tour of Antigua with an English-speaking guide. The city lies in the broad Panchoy Valley, between the Agua, Acatenango and Fuego volcanoes.

Antigua was founded in 1543 as Guatemala's third capital and was known as Santiago de Guatemala. The country's first three capitals were named after Saint James the Apostle, known in Spanish as Santiago. After the devastating Santa Marta earthquake of 1773, the capital was moved to what is now Guatemala City. Two years later, the former capital became known as Antigua Guatemala, meaning “Old Guatemala”.

The tour starts at the main square in the historic centre and takes in the city's principal landmarks.

Overnight at the hotel.
